title: TMT-based Quantification LNH treated with incomptine A
projectDescription: Summary In this project, 2717 proteins were identified. The fold-change cutoff was set when proteins with quantitative ratios above 1.5 or below 1/1.5 are deemed significant.
sampleProcessingProtocol: 1.1 Chemicals and Instrumentation TMT6plex Isobaric Label Reagent Set, Pierce Quantitative Colorimetric Peptide Assay, was purchased from Thermo Fisher Science. Triethylammonium bicarbonate buffer (1.0 M, pH 8.5Â±0.1), Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine hydrochloride solution (0.5 M, pH 7.0), iodoacetamide (IAA), formic acid (FA), acetonitrile (ACN), methanol, were purchased from Sigma (St. Louis, MO, USA). Trypsin from bovine pancreas was purchased from Promega (Madison, WI, USA). Ultrapure water was prepared from a Millipore purification system (Billerica, MA, USA). an Ultimate 3000 nano UHPLC system (Thermo Scientific, Waltham, MA) coupled online to a Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific) equipped with a Nanospray Flex Ion Source (Thermo Scientific). 1.2 Sample Preparation 1.2.1 Protein Extraction 1) Add an appropriate amount of tissue lysis buffer and lyse the tissues by using TissueLyser. 2) Centrifuge at 12000 rpm for 15 min at low temperature and transfer the supernatant to a new EP tube. 3) Determine the protein concentration by BCA kit. 1.2.2 Protein Digestion 1) Transfer 100 ug protein per sample into a new microcentrifuge tube. 2) To each sample tube, reduced by 10 mM TCEP at 56Â°C for 1 h. 3) Alkylated by 20 mM IAA at room temperature in dark for 1h. 4) Add free trypsin into the protein solution at a ratio of 1:50, and the solution was incubated at 37Â°C overnight. 5) Lyophilize the extracted peptides to near dryness. Re-dissolve the sample with 100 mM TEAB. 1.2.3 Peptide Labeling 1) Immediately before use, equilibrate the TMT Label Reagents to room temperature. Add 41 Î¼L of anhydrous acetonitrile to each tube. Allow the reagent to dissolve for 5 minutes with occasional vortex. Briefly centrifuge the tube to gather the solution. 2) Transfer the samples to the TMT Reagent vial as Table 1.1. Incubate the reaction for 1 hour at room temperature. 3) Add 8Î¼L of 5% hydroxylamine to the sample and incubate for 15 minutes to quench the reaction. 4) Combine samples at equal amounts in new microcentrifuge tube 1.2.4 Fractionation of the Sample Fractionation of the labeled peptides with 6 components using HPLC. 1.3 Nano LC-MS/MS Analysis 1.3.1 nanoLC Nanoflow UPLC: Ultimate 3000 nano UHPLC system (ThermoFisher Scientific, USA); Nanocolumn: trapping column (PepMap C18, 100Ã… , 100 Î¼mÃ—2 cm, 5Î¼m) and an analytical column (PepMap C18, 100Ã…, 75 Î¼mÃ—50 cm, 2Î¼m); Loaded sample volume: 2 Î¼g Mobile phase: A: 0.1% formic acid in water; B: 0.1% formic acid in 80% acetonitrile. Total flow rate : 250 nL/min LC linear gradient: from 5 to 7% buffer B in 2 min, from 7% to 20% buffer B in 80 min, from 20% to 40% buffer B in 35 min, then from 40% to 90% buffer B in 4 min. 1.3.2 Mass Spectrometry For TMT-labeled samples, the full scan was performed between 350â€“1,650 m/z at the resolution 120,000 at 200 Th, the automatic gain control target for the full scan was set to 3e6. The MS/MS scan was operated in Top 15 mode using the following settings: resolution 30,000 at 200 Th; automatic gain control target 1e5; normalized collision energy at 32%; isolation window of 1.2 Th; charge sate exclusion: unassigned, 1, > 6; dynamic exclusion 40 s.
dataProcessingProtocol: 1.4 Data Analysis The 6 raw MS files were analyzed and searched against mouse protein database based on the species of the samples using Maxquant (1.6.2.6). The parameters were set as follows: the protein modifications were carbamidomethylation (C) (fixed), oxidation (M) (variable), TMT-6Plex; the enzyme specificity was set to trypsin; the maximum missed cleavages were set to 2; the precursor ion mass tolerance was set to 10 ppm, and MS/MS tolerance was 0.6 Da.
